input: Learn basic watercolor techniques on YouTube

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Watercolor is broad — knowing whether they want specific techniques (wet-on-wet, washes, blending) or a general overview changes which videos to prioritize.
Whether this is for themselves or to teach someone else (e.g., a child) affects the level, tone, and style of content to seek out.
Knowing whether they are a complete beginner or have some drawing/painting background determines where in a curriculum they should start.
How much time they can dedicate per week shapes whether they need short standalone tutorials or a structured multi-week series.
Whether they already have watercolor supplies or still need to buy them affects whether 'supply guidance' videos should be part of the plan.
Some learners prefer structured playlists with a single teacher; others prefer exploring multiple creators. This changes how the watchlist is organised.
Understanding what 'done' looks like — e.g., completing a first finished painting, mastering specific strokes, or just feeling confident — defines a clear endpoint for the plan.

gold.taskTitle: Learn basic watercolor techniques on YouTube
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to learn foundational watercolor painting skills by watching YouTube videos.

questions.title: Which specific techniques do you most want to learn first?
questions.description: E.g., flat washes, wet-on-wet blending, gradients, loose florals, landscapes — or just a general beginner overview.

questions.title: Are you a complete beginner or have some prior painting experience?
questions.description: Knowing your starting point determines whether to begin with absolute basics or skip foundational content.

questions.title: Are you learning this for yourself or someone else?
questions.description: E.g., personal hobby, teaching a child, a class project — affects the level and tone of recommended content.

questions.title: How many hours per week can you dedicate to watching and practicing?
questions.description: Determines whether the plan uses quick standalone tutorials or a longer structured series spread over weeks.

questions.title: Do you already have watercolor supplies, or do you still need to buy them?
questions.description: If supplies are needed, beginner supply-guide videos should be included early in the plan before technique tutorials.

questions.title: Do you prefer following one teacher's series or sampling multiple creators?
questions.description: Shapes whether to build a single-channel playlist or a curated mix of the best standalone videos across YouTube.

questions.title: What would completing this goal successfully look like for you?
questions.description: E.g., finishing one complete painting, confidently using three techniques, or posting work online — defines a clear, measurable endpoint.
